nom: medicube 3H Overnight Drying Lotion for Targeted Spot Care

segments.sensitive: The one reviewer who describes highly sensitive, reactive skin reports a cluster of red, irritated blemishes completely cleared with no visible redness by the next morning; another reviewer without sensitive skin herself cautions that people with sensitive skin should be careful with this product.
segments.mature: The one reviewer who names her skin as mature, 52 and post-menopausal, reports the treatment calms breakouts by morning without leaving her skin overly dry, which she says matters more for mature skin than for other formulas she has tried.
segments.combination: The one reviewer with combination skin, an oily T-zone and a dry, tretinoin-irritated chin, reports it calms cystic acne overnight without drying out the surrounding skin.
segments.dry: The one reviewer with dry, mature skin reports the treatment works without leaving her skin feeling overly dry, unlike some other drying lotions she has tried.

concerns.blemishes: This is the effect nearly every reviewer reports success with: pimples, cystic acne, whiteheads and closed comedones look noticeably smaller, less inflamed or gone by the next morning after a single overnight application, including on hormonal and cystic acne. Against this, one critical reviewer says it burned her skin and specifically warns not to use it on cystic acne, and another says it left visible white residue inside her pores for about a day.
concerns.redness: Many reviewers credit the calamine in the formula with visibly calming redness and inflammation around a blemish within one overnight use, including reviewers who call themselves sensitive or reactive; no reviewer reports the product itself causing new redness, aside from the one critical review describing a burn.
concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers specifically note that, unlike other drying lotions, this one does not leave the skin around the treated spot feeling painfully dry, flaky or crusty the next morning; none report it drying out their skin more broadly.

aspects.libelle: Must not be shaken; apply the settled sediment with a cotton swab

extraits.texte: I would put zero stars if I could. Burned my skin, do not use on cystic acne.

It definitely works, but it leaves white residue in the pores. It doesn’t come off with water, it’s down deep in the pores and looks like little white dots. I don’t have particularly large pores. Granted it goes away after a day or so, but that’s annoying. Don’t think I’ll be ordering this again.

extraits.titre: Like the Cult-Favorite Mario Badescu — But I Actually Like This One Better
extraits.texte: I’m 52 and post-menopausal with dry, mature skin, so I don’t deal with breakouts as often as I used to — but when I do, I want something that’s effective without being overly harsh or drying. This Medicube 3H Overnight Drying Lotion really impressed me. If you’re familiar with the Mario Badescu Drying Lotion (the cult classic), this is very similar in concept — but honestly, I like this one better. First, it works. When I apply this directly to a spot at night, I usually notice that by morning the area looks calmer, less red, and less inflamed. It doesn’t completely erase everything overnight, but it definitely speeds up healing in a noticeable way. What makes this one stand out for me is that it feels gentler and more skin-friendly, which is important for mature skin. Some drying lotions can be too aggressive and leave the surrounding area flaky or irritated. This one helps calm breakouts without making my skin feel overly dry. I also like the ingredient combination here — calamine, centella, and tea tree — which makes it feel more soothing while still being effective. It’s a nice balance between treatment and calming care. The texture is exactly what you expect from a drying lotion — you dip a cotton swab into the pink sediment and apply directly to the spot. It’s easy to use and dries quickly. Another plus is that a little goes a long way, so even though the bottle looks small, it should last quite a while. That makes this a good value, especially considering how effective

extraits.titre: Best drying lotion I have tried yet!
extraits.texte: For reference, I have combo skin (oily t-zone and dry chin/cheeks), with hormonal acne. I use tretinoin roughly 3-4 days per week to help with the hormonal acne on my, chin and jawline, this has caused me to have some dry patches in those areas. I do not have sensitive skin or eyes, as I can use direct acids and most fragrances without irritation. I also have some slight pitting from acne scaring. I prefer unscented or lightly scented products and light weight/gel textured products when possible. Medicube NEVER FAILS ME!! I absolutely love this Overnight Drying Lotion. I have been using the Eradikate Drying Lotion, but that is $30 and Medicube is $15, great value! I love the design of this bottle as well, it makes it easier to not spill and to get the excess off the qtip. I do not feel like this dying lotion dries out the skin around my acne, which is a step up from what I was using before. This helps my cystic acne feel much better by the next morning. If you have had a cystic acne spot, you know how badly they can hurt. It also helps the scab heal faster when I have given in and popped my pimples instead of wearing a patch. I cannot even feel this on my skin. There is a strong alcohol smell, but no Sulphur smell, and the smell goes away as soon as it dries down, which is almost immediately. If you are looking for a drying lotion that will not break the bank, this is the one!

extraits.titre: The ultimate "reset button" for sensitive skin flare-ups
extraits.texte: As a regular product tester with highly sensitive skin, I frequently deal with inflammation and irritation from new formulas. This product has been an absolute lifesaver. If you’re old enough to remember the scent of calamine lotion from childhood (the chicken pox remedy), you’ll recognize the smell and the pink tint from this bottle immediately. I was able to test the product upon arrival because of a cluster of red, irritated blemishes that had been lingering for three days. I applied a small dab directly onto the infected area, and it dried rather quickly onto my skin, anlmost immediately after applied as if I hadn't applied any product at all. That is how light weight it feels and quickly it dries onto the skin. By the next morning, the irritation was completely gone with no visible signs of redness. I tried it again on the other side where I had a similar breakout with the same overnight results. It’s rare to find something that works this fast on active inflammation. If your skin is reactive like mine, this belongs in your permanent skincare "first aid kit."

I have hormonal acne that I hate and that can be deep. I also have a hard time not picking at it and trying to get it out. This stuff is amazing. I put it on as the last step of my skin care routine and have never felt any irritation but that also means there could be a good layer of products between my skin and this product. That being said it also hasn’t interacted negatively to any of my other skin care products. I only use it at night. It dries quickly and I just leave it on. By the next morning I always see a significant difference in the size, redness, irritation and pressure of the acne spot. This will remain a staple in my skin care routine.

extraits.titre: Superior version of an old favorite
extraits.texte: This was such a throwback product for me! I’ve thankfully aged out of regular breakouts, but my daughter is just getting into that phase where things seem to appear overnight, everything from little whiteheads to those big, stubborn closed comedones that literally look angry. So I figured I’d introduce her to the same style of drying lotion I used as a teen. And yes, it’s the classic no-shake, pink powder-in-alcohol situation. You dip a Q-tip straight down into the bottom layer and dab it on. Very nostalgic. The ingredient list is exactly what you’d expect from this category, with a few upgrades. Alcohol is the base, which helps dry out the lesion and keeps the formula antimicrobial. Calamine (zinc oxide + iron oxides) is doing a lot of the heavy lifting in terms of calming inflammation and reducing redness. There’s also salicylic acid in there to help clear out pores and break down the buildup inside those deeper clogs. Sulfur shows up as well, which has both antibacterial and keratolytic properties, so it helps dry things out and speed up resolution. This ingredient mix means it works on whiteheads, comedones, and even blackheads. What makes this feel more modern is the addition of things like centella, beta-glucan, ceramide NP, and a few humectants. Those don’t turn it into a hydrating product by any means, but they do take the edge off so you’re not left with that angry, cracked halo around the spot the next morning. And it works. Even on those bigger, deeper “shiner” zit
